text:
maya: paging oncall — noticing p99 generator latency jump from ~220ms -> 1.8s across eu-west GPU shared-pool around 18:00 UTC. Affected routes: /v1/stream and /v1/generate. Streaming stalls for some customers. :alarm:
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421. Paging #eng-oncall.
ryan: I see correlated spike in host i/o wait and blkio throttle counters on node gpool-eu-14. p95 also moved up but p99 is worst.
samira: streaming stall traces show lots of KV-cache evictions for the same tenant id=t-9843, unusual working set. Possibly noisy neighbor with big ephemeral context.
alex: putting initial mitigation: set tenant t-9843 to isolation pool (reserved gpu pool) and reduce their max_concurrency to 2. Doing `redwoodctl tenant move --id t-9843 --pool reserved-eu-west-01` now.
maya: thanks alex — what about cgroup fixes? infra-bot / root cause diagnostics?
infra-bot: observed cgroup blkio.weight drops on the host; top IO pids show /usr/bin/inference_worker (tid 12345) reading large checkpoint shards. blkio.stats: throttled_time increased by 4.2s in last 5m.
ryan: trying soft-evict of tenant processes from gpool-eu-14: `systemctl kill --signal=SIGTERM inference-tenant-t-9843` (graceful). If that doesn't free I/O quick, escalate to hard kill.
samira: can we set a temporary io.limit for tenant slices instead? `cgset -r blkio.weight=300 /tenant_t9843` (current default 1000 on reserved). Will apply on host and coord with runtime to prevent stalls.
alex: applied cgset on gpool-eu-14 for t-9843, weight -> 300. early telemetry shows host iowait dropping. p95 returning to ~320ms, p99 still around 1.2s.
maya: good. re-route streaming sessions to dedicated streaming nodes for impacted customers while we observe. `route set --from pool shared-eu-west --to pool streaming-dedicated-eu` (rolling, will keep sessions for <30s).
ryan: started reroute; about 35% of in-flight streams failed to gracefully reconnect — we triggered auto-retry. Customer impact: several mid-size tenants saw degraded streams for ~45-90s each.
samira: capturing a sample trace for the worst offender (t-9843): repeated large batched requests with long context (~40k tokens). This caused KV cache churn on shared GPUs. We should set a per-tenant max_context_tokens and fallback to smaller context for shared pools.
maya: agreed — short term: throttle max_context_tokens for shared pools to 16k, and add a guard that redirects >16k jobs to dedicated or queue. I'll file a follow-up config change.
alex: also increased autoscale burst for reserved-eu-west-01 by +2 nodes to absorb any noisy bursts while we stabilize.
infra-bot: node gpool-eu-14 iowait back to baseline. Token throughput per-second recovered. No further blkio throttle events in last 4m.
ryan: marking mitigation as successful for now. Will keep incident open for postmortem and follow-up tasks: quota guard, context cap, stronger cgroup defaults, better eviction heuristics, and customer notification draft.
maya: oncall handoff at 20:00 UTC to @ryan. I'll prepare a short blameless summary and customer-facing note for CS.
samira: saved logs and traces to /var/log/incidents/3654321000/ and uploaded collected profiles to s3://redwood-incidents/3654321000/traces.tar.gz.
alex: notes for postmortem - root cause: noisy tenant with very large contexts causing KV cache thrash and heavy checkpoint reads -> host io pressure -> cgroup throttling -> streaming tail latency.
maya: action items (short):
- set shared-pool context cap 16k (maya)
- implement per-tenant io throttle by default (ryan)
- add auto-evict policy if blkio.throttle > X ms in 1m (samira)
- customer note draft (maya -> cs review)
- full postmortem (owner: samira)
ryan: I'll keep monitoring for 1h post-handoff, will re-open if p99 > 1s again.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 status updated -> MITIGATED (live mitigations applied).
maya: closing thread for now; will attach postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:
